subject: general
question: Tracheid is part of which plant tissue?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tracheids** are elongated, tube-like cells with thick, **lignified walls** and tapering ends that serve as the primary conducting elements of the **Xylem**.
 
• They are **dead cells** at maturity, meaning they lack **protoplasm**, which allows them to function efficiently as hollow tubes for water transport. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• The main function of tracheids is the **conduction of water and minerals** from the roots to various parts of the plant, such as the stem and leaves.
 
• In **Pteridophytes** and **Gymnosperms**, tracheids are the only water-conducting elements, whereas **Angiosperms** (flowering plants) possess both tracheids and **vessels**.
 
• Apart from conduction, the thick, lignified walls of tracheids provide significant **mechanical support** to the plant body, helping it stand upright.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Xylem (Complex Permanent Tissue):**

 
 
• The term **Xylem** was introduced by **Carl Nägeli** in **1858**.
 
• It is composed of four distinct types of elements: **Tracheids**, **Vessels**, **Xylem Parenchyma**, and **Xylem Fibers**.
 
• **Xylem Parenchyma** is the only **living component** of the xylem and is responsible for storing food materials like starch and fats.
 
• **Vessels** are long cylindrical structures with perforated end walls, forming continuous channels for water flow, a characteristic feature of **Angiosperms**.
 
 
 
• **Phloem:**
 
 
• **Phloem** is responsible for the **translocation of organic food** (sucrose) from the leaves (source) to other parts of the plant (sink). ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• It consists of **Sieve tubes**, **Companion cells**, **Phloem parenchyma**, and **Phloem fibers**.
 
• Unlike xylem, phloem transport is **bidirectional**, allowing nutrients to move both up and down the plant.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cuticle:**

 
 
• The **Cuticle** is a protective, waxy, and water-repellent layer covering the **epidermis** of leaves, young shoots, and other aerial plant organs. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Its primary function is to **minimize water loss** through transpiration and protect the plant against **pathogens** and mechanical injury.
 
 
 
• **Bark:**
 
 
• **Bark** is a non-technical term used to describe all tissues **outside the vascular cambium**, including the secondary phloem, periderm, and phellogen. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• It forms during **secondary growth** in woody plants and acts as a protective outer covering against **environmental stress** and physical damage.
 
 
 
• **Structural Differences:**
 
 
• **Tracheids** possess **pits** (thin areas in the cell wall) through which water passes from cell to cell, whereas **vessels** have **perforation plates** at their ends for more rapid conduction.
 
• The presence of **Lignin** in tracheid walls is a crucial evolutionary adaptation that allowed plants to grow tall by providing **structural rigidity**.
